question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{a}^{2}-2ab+{b}^{2}=(a-b)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
9{y}^{2}-6y+1.
$$

First, we write both the quadratic term and the constant term as perfect squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3y)^{2}-6y+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3y)^{2}-2(3y)+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the middle parentheses $(3y)$ as a product of $3y$ and $1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3y)^{2}-2(3y\cdot 1)+(1)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=3y$ and $b=1.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}(3y-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
